catalog_quote: Acentuación: El acento ortográfico, por los fines de este Vocabulario, se escribe solamente en las sílabas tónicas de los radicales de las palabras variables, y en palabras de dos y tres sílabas no graves. El acento de los sufijos se observará en el Apéndice Notas Gramaticales y como es casi constante, no es necesario escribirlo. La primera sílaba tónica de una palabra lleva más fuerza que las demás, y siempre es una de las dos primeras sílabas de la palabra.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Acentuación: El acento ortográfico, por los fines de este Vocabulario, se escribe solamente en las sílabas tónicas de los radicales de las palabras variables, y en palabras de dos y tres sílabas no graves. El acento de los sufijos se observará en el Apéndice Notas Gramaticales y como es casi constante, no es necesario escribirlo. La primera sílaba tónica de una palabra lleva más fuerza que las demás, y siempre es una de las dos primeras sílabas de la palabra.
new_statements.translation: Accentuation: The orthographic accent, for the purposes of this Vocabulary, is written only on the stressed syllables of the roots of inflectable words, and on words of two and three syllables that are not paroxytone. The stress of the suffixes will be seen in the Appendix 'Grammatical Notes' and, since it is almost constant, it is not necessary to write it. The first stressed syllable of a word carries more force than the others, and is always one of the first two syllables of the word.
new_statements.citation: Tuggy, John. 2008 [1966]. Vocabulario Candoshi de Loreto. Serie Lingüística Peruana 2, 2nd ed. Lima: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. Apéndice I, Ortología, 'Acentuación', p. 235 (PDF page 243).
new_statements.locator: Apéndice I Ortología, section 'Acentuación', printed p. 235 (running header misprinted 'Apéndice II'); p. 243 of the archive.org scan; supporting: alphabet examples p. 233 (PDF 241), Apéndice II Notas Gramaticales p. 240 (PDF 248)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Re-rendered PDF page 243 of myself (page render; text is empty, 1 byte from extracted text) and read the page scan: printed p. 235, running header misprinted "Apéndice II" though it is inside Apéndice I Ortología (pp. 232-236). The paragraph headed "Acentuación:" reads word for word as quoted: "El acento ortográfico, por los fines de este Vocabulario, se escribe solamente en las sílabas tónicas de los radicales de las palabras variables, y en palabras de dos y tres sílabas no graves. El acento de los sufijos se observará en el Apéndice Notas Gramaticales y como es casi constante, no es necesario escribirlo. La primera sílaba tónica de una palabra lleva más fuerza que las demás, y siempre es…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Words may carry more than one stressed syllable; the leftmost stressed syllable is the strongest (primary) and always falls on the first or second syllable of the word. Which of the two it is must be learned per root (hence the orthographic accent on roots), with the Spanish-style convention that unmarked 2-3-syllable words are paroxytone; suffix stress is nearly constant and not. Provisional reading: lexically placed primary stress within an initial two-syllable window (initial or peninitial).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Implied but not analysed: example words carry two written accents (chóró 'choro monkey', kápá 'thorn', máká 'snake', gópogó 'snail', dáraná 'lizard', p. 233); suffixes have their own 'almost constant' stress (p. 235); the first stressed syllable is stronger than the later ones.
new_statements.exceptions: Morphological shift: for n3-type noun roots the 3rd-person possessive form 'se cambia el acento principal a la primera sílaba del radical y se pierde la sílaba anteriormente acentuada' (main accent moves to the first syllable of the root and the previously accented syllable is lost) (p. 240). Vowel loss at unstressed morpheme junctures (p. 236).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('palabra'), stated as an orthographic convention for the dictionary's citation forms; distinguishes root stress from suffix stress (unwritten, nearly constant). Author is an SIL fieldworker; no phonetic/phonological analysis, no minimal pairs. The 2008 edition reprints the 1966 text.
new_statements.identity_note: Tuggy's Vocabulario describes 'Candoshi de Loreto', i.e. the Candoshi proper (Murato) rather than the Shapra (Chápara) of the Río Morona, whom Tuggy names as the other division of the same people (p. v); Glottolog has no separate code for Shapra, so the record belongs under cand1248 with the dialect flagged as Candoshi/Murato. Overall's 2023 chapter uses the name Kandozi-Chapra for the same language.

new_statements.quote: La unidad /P¹/ tiene el rasgo distintivo de un solo acento principal que se manifiesta en la primera sílaba de la palabra F [+acento inicial]. (...) La unidad /P²/ tiene el acento principal en la segunda sílaba de la palabra F [-acento inicial]. (Las palabras que manifiestan la unidad /P²/ aparecen con acento agudo en la transcripción fonémica.) El acento principal siempre aparece dentro de los límites del radical gramatical de la palabra. La configuración fonética de la palabra es impresionante, pues en una de las dos primeras sílabas se escucha el golpe marcado del acento principal seguido por un acento de segunda intensidad en la última sílaba.
new_statements.translation: The unit /P1/ has the distinctive feature of a single main stress realized on the first syllable of the phonological word [+initial stress]. (...) The unit /P2/ has the main stress on the second syllable of the phonological word [-initial stress]. (Words manifesting /P2/ appear with an acute accent in the phonemic transcription.) The main stress always falls within the limits of the grammatical root of the word. The phonetic shape of the word is striking: on one of the first two syllables one hears the marked beat of the main stress, followed by a second-degree stress on the last syllable.
new_statements.citation: Tuggy, John. 1981. Un estudio fonológico del discurso candoshi. In M. R. Wise & A. Stewart (eds.), Cohesión y enfoque en textos y discursos (Serie Lingüística Peruana 17), 217-273. Yarinacocha: ILV. (English: A discourse phonology of Candoshi, in Discourse Phonology, 5-28, 1981.)
new_statements.locator: Section 2.2.6 'La palabra F', p. 228 (also 2.2.7 'La sílaba', p. 229; Apéndice, p. 245; Conclusiones p. 243)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (273 pp. 217, 228, 243-245, 253, 270 myself; also read the saved page scan and the scanned file lines 460-522). p. 217 is the chapter title page 'UN ESTUDIO FONOLOGICO DEL DISCURSO CANDOSHI, John Tuggy'. p. 228, section 2.2.6 'La palabra F', carries the quoted passage word for word: '/P1/ tiene el rasgo distintivo de un solo acento principal que se manifiesta en la primera silaba de la palabra F [+acento inicial]'.. '/P2/ tiene el acento principal en la segunda silaba de la palabra F [-acento inicial]'.. 'El acento principal siempre aparece dentro de los limites del radical gramatical de la palabra'.. 'en una de las dos primeras silabas se escucha el golpe marcado del acento principa…
new_statements.relation_note: Catalog record (world-r2) has an empty rule; the existing statement (Tuggy 2008 [1966] Vocabulario, p. 235) only says the orthographic accent is written on the tonic syllable of roots, read as lexical. Tuggy 1981 is compatible (stress lexical, root-internal) and adds the precise system: a binary lexical contrast first- vs second-syllable main stress (initial two-syllable window), fixed secondary stress on the final syllable, morphologically conditioned tertiary stresses from suffixes, a syllable-type restriction on second-syllable stress, and non-contrastive pitch tied to stress and vowel length. No contradiction.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The phonological word (1-7 syllables) carries one main stress that is contrastively either on the first syllable (/P1/, unmarked) or on the second syllable (/P2/, written with an acute); the choice is lexical but confined to a two-syllable initial window and the main stress always lies inside the grammatical root. p. 229 adds that /P2/ (second-syllable stress) is possible only when the word begins with a V, VC, CV or CVC syllable (not with CCV/CCVC/CCCV/CCCVC onsets). Syllable pitch is tied to stress (rises/falls with syllable intensity; falls markedly on geminate vowels and diphthongs), i.e. tone is not contrastive at word level; word-final syllables carry clause/sentence intonation.
new_statements.secondary_stress: A secondary (second-intensity) stress falls on the word-final syllable; between main and final stress there may be several syllables with tertiary stress or none, their placement 'condicionado morfológicamente por las propiedades inherentes de los sufijos' (morphologically conditioned by the suffixes); when main stress and the final secondary stress would coincide (short words) the secondary is eliminated (p. 228). Example: zi'taminanàarí (longest word in text 52Ts11) vs 'da (shortest).
new_statements.exceptions: /P2/ restricted to words whose first syllable is V, VC, CV or CVC (p. 229); discourse-level emphasis can add strong intensity on the nucleus of a word (3.2), and some lexemes carry idiosyncratic voice-quality features (e.g. pákéci 'pequeño', p. 234-235), which the author excludes from the phonological structure. Transcription convention (p. 245): 'Acento principal de la palabra: acento ortográfico solamente cuando la segunda sílaba de la palabra es acentuada; el acento en la primera sílaba no se marca.'
new_statements.identity_note: Tuggy 1981 analyses three recorded Candoshi texts: 52Ts11 and 11Ts1 narrated by Tsirimbo Tariri Marazo (recorded Nov 1960 by the author) and 42AMik by Mikaya Tirko de Kasho (recorded April 1975 by Sheila Tuggy) (Notas, p. 270); the language is 'candoshi' = Candoshi-Shapra [cbu], cand1248, per the SIL record 30027. No Shapra/Chapra dialect distinction is drawn.
